description_full: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates membership warehouse clubs on the eastern half of the United States. The company offers groceries, fresh food, general merchandise, gasoline, and other ancillary services. It sells its products through its clubs; the BJs.com website; and its mobile app. The company was formerly known as Beacon Holding Inc. and changed its name to BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. in February 2018. BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts.

financial_summary: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, I is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $13.9B market cap on $21.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 7% cost of capital — a 19-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $328M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.78× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 19× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 4% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Defensive median (7%).

mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 6% over the past year excluding the latest month.

Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 56% above its 10-year median.

ROE of 26% is amplified by 3.4x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.4x net debt to EBITDA ($46.2M of cash against $519.1M of debt), with interest covered 19.3x.
The current ratio of 0.75 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.6% over 3 years and 6.8% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 64% of profits supports about 16.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -12.8% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.00, a backlog worth 0% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 16%.
